This peptide was further refined to its minimal functional unit required through alanine substitution and deletion scanning to the cyclic pentapeptide cyclo-[CPFVC] (Hall et al., 2007). However, because free monovalent peptides were less effec- tive than those presented on phage, subsequent research (Hall et al., 2008) shifted towards presenting peptides in a multivalent format on nanoparticles and targeting the orthohantavirus glycoproteins directly rather than the host b3-integrin receptor. The three most potent binders of the virion were selected and attached to 100 nm nanoparticles to create a multivalent inhibitor. When the peptide CLVRNLAWC was presented on a nanoparticle at a 4:1 ratio, its inhibition of SNV jumped from 9% (as a free peptide) to 32.5%. However, the peptide CQATTARNC achieved an even higher efficacy, with inhibition surpassing 50% when the nanoparticle- to-virus ratio was increased to 20:1 (Hall et al., 2008). Building on these strategies, the research was expanded to Andes virus (ANDV). Using a similar approach, Hall et al. (2009) eluted the peptide library from purified ANDV particles using monoclonal antibodies (mAbs) against the Gn and Gc glycoproteins. A major finding in this study was the combined use of peptides that targeted different Gn- and Gc-specific sequences resulted in synergistic inhibition (anti-Gc/Gn peptides CMQSAAAHC and CTVGPTRSC) of infec- tion that was significantly more powerful than single-peptide treatments, emphasizing the benefit of targeting multiple viral epitopes (Hall et al., 2009). Lastly, to search for peptidomimetic molecules to block SNV infection, Hall et al. (2010) used the 3D structure of the previously refined pentapeptide cyclo-[CPFVC], in a ligand-based virtual screening approach to evaluate over 600,000 small molecules. This transition from biological peptides to drug- like peptidomimetics identified compounds such as G319–0078 and 8012-0652, which were 2,000 times more potent than the original cyclic peptides. These molecules demonstrated high-affinity inhibi- tion in the nanomolar range in vitro (EC50 values between 1.3 - 2.5 nM) (Hall et al., 2010), successfully evolving the initial lead into a highly potent preclinical candidate warranting further in vivo evaluation. Another distinct strategy to prevent infection focuses on dis- rupting the viral membrane fusion process. Because the orthohantavirus Gc glycoprotein functions as a class II fusion protein, completing membrane fusion requires a major structural relocation of Domain III (DIII) to achieve the post-fusion state (Barriga et al., 2016; Arata-Salas et al., 2026). Exploiting this mechanical vulnerability, Barriga et al. (2016) demonstrated that viral entry can be successfully blocked using recombinant fragments and synthetic peptides derived from the Gc DIII and stem region. These fragments allow initial Gc trimerization to proceed but ultimately inhibit the pathway by preventing membrane hemifusion and fusion pore formation (Barriga et al., 2016). The recombinant DIII fragment inhibited ANDV fusion by around 70% at 25 μM and demonstrated cross-reactivity by reducing PUUV-mediated fusion by 50%. Even greater potency was observed with the R2 peptide, derived from the C-terminal part of the Gc stem region, which inhibited ANDV fusion by up to 95% in vitro (Barriga et al., 2016). Although efficacy dropped to a 70% cross-reduction (at 20 μM) against PUUV-mediated fusion (Barriga et al., 2016) due to its high genetic divergence between the two viruses, it still demonstrates significant cross-protective potential. Another very potent cell-entry inhibitor is Griffithsin (GRFT), an algae-derived lectin that has demonstrated high efficacy against several enveloped viruses such as coronaviruses, retroviruses, lentiviruses, flaviviruses, hepaciviruses, paramyxoviruses, and her- pesviruses, with the notable exclusion of gamma- and delta-retro- viruses. Interestingly, GRFT is also effective against the non- enveloped human papillomavirus (HPV), where it acts during a late step in the viral entry process rather than during initial attachment (O’Keefe et al., 2010; Lusvarghi and Bewley, 2016). In vivo administration of GRFT demonstrated clear therapeutic effi- cacy, significantly mitigating disease severity and reducing mortality in lethal SARS-CoV infection models (O’Keefe et al., 2010). Highlighting its strong translational potential, GRFT has also advanced to phase I clinical trials against human immunodeficiency virus (HIV-1) infections (ClinicalTrials.gov Identifiers: NCT04032717, NCT02875119). In addition to potent inhibition of ANDV entry (Shrivastava-Ranjan et al., 2020), found that a synthetic trimeric variant (3mGRFT) possessing nine oligosaccha- ride-binding sites demonstrated even greater in vitro potency against ANDV and SNV. However, in contrast to its post-infection efficacy seen in other viral models (Lusvarghi and Bewley, 2016), the authors observed that GRFT lacked potent inhibitory activity against ANDV post-infection. While GRFT showed in vitro effec- tivity against New World hantaviruses (Shrivastava-Ranjan et al., 2020), the lectin inhibited HTNV in vivo and provided partial protection in suckling mice infected with HTNV (Zhao et al., 2022). Moreover, GRFT can be produced on a large scale and can be easily purified, highlighting its potential as an antiviral candidate for further preclinical testing against orthohantaviruses (Zhao et al., 2022). Exploring natural host defense proteins, bovine lactoferrin (LF) has demonstrated significant efficacy as a viral inhibitor against SEOV. LF prevents initial viral adsorption and adhesion, likely by interacting with cellular glycosaminoglycans such as heparin, or by sterically hindering the virus from binding to host b-integrin and lectin receptors (Murphy et al., 2000, 2001). Importantly, LF has no antiviral effect once the virus entered the host cell. In vivo, prophylactic administration of LF one day prior to orthohantavirus inoculation improved survival rates in mice up to 70% (at 160 mg/ kg), with a double-administration regimen enhancing survival to over 94%. Furthermore, when prophylactic LF treatment was combined with subsequent ribavirin administration, the two agents functioned synergistically, profoundly reducing viral shed- ding and completely inhibiting viral protein expression (Murphy et al., 2000, 2001). Discovered through a high-throughput screening of over 2,300 approved drugs and traditional Chinese medicines, cepharanthine (CEP), which is a compound isolated from Stephania cephalantha Hayata, has emerged as a highly potent viral entry and membrane fusion inhibitor. In vitro, CEP inhibited HTNV pseudovirus (EC50 value of 0.9 μM) and reduced viral nucleic acid copies by 73% at 20 μM. In vivo, administering CEP to Balb/c mice five hours post- infection significantly reduced infection by 93% (at 90 mg/kg/day) and 94% (at 180 mg/kg/day). Given its established safety profile, Kocabiyik et al. 10.3389/fcimb.2026.1972830 Frontiers in Cellular and Infection Microbiology frontiersin.org 03 CEP represents a high-priority candidate for repurposing and advancement into human clinical trials against orthohantaviruses (Wen et al., 2022). Viral replication and polymerase inhibitors Ribavirin (1-b- D-ribofuranosyl-1H-1,2,4-triazole-3- carboxamide; RBV), a synthetic guanosine nucleoside analogue, serves as the historical benchmark for anti-hantaviral therapy (Sidwell et al., 1972). Once it is transported into host cells, RBV is rapidly phosphorylated into metabolites such as RBV-5’-mono- phosphate (RBV-MP) and RBV-5’-triphosphate (RBV-TP). While RBV-MP inhibits inosine monophosphate dehydrogenase (IMPDH), resulting in a decrease in intracellular GTP levels, RBV-TP selectively interacts with the viral RdRp as its primary mechanism of action (Severson et al., 2003; Sun et al., 2007). The incorporation of RBV leads to accumulation of genomic errors, and thus to dramatic loss of virus viability (“error catastrophe”) (Severson et al., 2003; Chung et al., 2007). Preclinical evaluation confirmed that early RBV administration reduces viral loads and prevents severe disease in suckling mouse models infected with Hantaan virus (HTNV) and hamster models infected with Andes virus (ANDV) (Huggins et al., 1986; Ogg et al., 2013). Clinically, intravenous RBV demonstrated efficacy in a double-blind, placebo- controlled trial of 242 patients with HTNV-induced HFRS, signif- icantly reducing hemorrhagic and overall mortality (Huggins et al., 1991). However, efficacy varies significantly across strains and clinical syndromes. In the context of HCPS caused by Andes virus (ANDV), intervention with RBV eliminated mortality com- pared to a 35% historical case-fatality rate and reduced the inci- dence of the severe cardiopulmonary phase from 84% to 57% (Strella et al., 2025). Conversely, in a larger placebo-controlled, double-blinded trial evaluating intravenous RBV for HCPS, the drug failed to demonstrate overall therapeutic efficacy, revealing no significant difference in survival (70% with RBV vs. 62% with placebo), nor in necessity of extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) between groups (Mertz et al., 2004). Trials in HFRS caused by Puumala virus (PUUV) also showed insufficient efficacy and safety of intravenous RBV, likely due to delayed drug administra- tion and weaker correlation between viral load and disease severity compared to HTNV infection (Malinin and Platonov, 2017). Despite its status as an established treatment for HFRS, the clinical utility of RBV is constrained by dose-limiting toxicities, most notably reversible hemolytic anemia, reported in 71% of recipients (Chapman et al., 1999; Jonsson et al., 2010). Furthermore, the lack of efficacy in HCPS and PUUV-caused HFRS is attributed to the rapid clinical progression of these diseases, which often leaves a narrow window for intervention before the onset of irreversible organ failure (Heyman et al., 2009; Vaheri et al., 2013a; Strella et al., 2025). Originally discovered by Toyama Chemical Co., Ltd., during a screening for anti-influenza compounds, the prodrug favipiravir (T- 705) has emerged as a potent viral replication inhibitor. Upon cellular entry, host enzymes convert favipiravir into its active form, favipiravir-RTP. This active metabolite functions as a purine nucleotide analogue that is incorporated into nascent viral RNA, inducing lethal mutagenesis in the viral genome (Furuta et al., 2009, 2017). Safronetz et al. (2013) have shown that favipiravir potently inhibited ANDV and SNV in vitro, and provided 100% survival in lethal ANDV hamster models when treatment was initiated before viremia, making it an important drug candidate for post-exposure prophylaxis. full_text_sections.full_text: Hantaviral therapeutics: life cycle targets and chemotherapeutic interventions Deren Zehra Kocabiyik 1,2, Jansen de Araujo 3, Edison Luiz Durigon 2,3* and Carsten Wrenger 1,2* 1Unit for Drug Discovery, Department of Parasitology, Institute of Biomedical Sciences, University of São Paulo, São Paulo, Brazil, 2Institut Pasteur de São Paulo, São Paulo, Brazil, 3Department of Microbiology, Institute of Biomedical Sciences, University of São Paulo, São Paulo, Brazil Orthohantaviruses represent a persistent global health threat, being responsible for life-threatening diseases such as Hemorrhagic Fever with Renal Syndrome (HFRS) and Hantavirus Cardiopulmonary Syndrome (HCPS). Despite high case fatality rates and recent outbreaks, there are currently no universally licensed antivirals or vaccines. Clinical management remains heavily reliant on supportive care and repurposed drugs, which often exhibit limited efficacy and dose-limiting toxicities. This review examines rational drug design strategies targeting critical steps in the viral life cycle, specifically Gn/Gc-mediated cellular entry and RNA- dependent RNA polymerase (RdRp)-driven genome replication. We evaluate the current landscape of viral inhibitors, including peptidomimetics, nucleoside analogues, and naturally derived compounds. To accelerate the discovery of novel treatments, we advocate for the integration of modern in silico screening to evaluate extensive chemical and natural product libraries. These broad com- pound collections offer a structurally diverse and largely untapped reservoir for antiviral development. Ultimately, expanding preclinical testing to include globally neglected variants will be essential to develop broad-spectrum hantaviral ther- apeutics capable of mitigating future epidemic threats. The high case fatality rate highlights that there are currently no universally licensed antivirals or vaccines against orthohantavirus infections (World Health Organization, 2026a). These rodent-borne pathogens belong to the family Hantaviridae, genus Orthohantavirus, and are enveloped, tri-segmented, single-stranded negative-sense RNA viruses (Jonsson et al., 2010). analysis.current_state: No universally licensed antivirals or vaccines exist, and clinical care is limited to supportive measures and repurposed drugs (A2).

analysis.summary_en: Background: Orthohantaviruses cause HFRS and HCPS, posing a persistent global health threat. Main directions: The review focuses on rational drug design targeting Gn/Gc entry and RdRp replication. Current state: No licensed antivirals or vaccines exist; care relies on supportive therapy and repurposed drugs. Gaps: Existing repurposed drugs have limited efficacy and toxicity, and many viral variants lack preclinical evaluation. Future research: Promote modern in silico screening of large chemical and natural‑product libraries to discover broad‑spectrum hantaviral therapeutics.

papers.title: Design and in silico evaluation of PV-GNProtecta: an mRNA multi-epitope vaccine candidate against Puumala virus using immunoinformatics and structural analysis.
papers.abstract: Puumala virus (PUUV), the principal causative agent of nephropathia epidemica (NE), poses a significant public health threat due to its zoonotic transmission, renal complications, and the lack of an approved vaccine. In this study, an immunoinformatics-driven mRNA multi-epitope vaccine, PV-GNProtecta, was designed using conserved regions of the viral glycoprotein (G) and nucleoprotein (N). Highly antigenic, non-allergenic, and non-toxic T-cell and B-cell epitopes were identified and assembled with appropriate adjuvants to enhance immunogenicity. Population coverage analysis suggested broad HLA responsiveness across diverse populations. The vaccine construct exhibited favorable physicochemical properties, including stability, solubility, and antigenicity. Structural validation predicted high model quality, with 95.5% of residues located in favored Ramachandran regions and an ERRAT score of 91.4. Molecular docking and MM-GBSA analyses predicted favorable computational interactions between PV-GNProtecta and TLR4, while a 100 ns molecular dynamics simulation provided computational insights into the dynamic behavior of the vaccine-TLR4 complex. Codon optimization suggested compatibility of the designed sequence with an Escherichia coli-based expression framework. Immune simulation predicted potential humoral and cellular immune response patterns, including changes in IgG, IFN-γ, and IL-2 levels. The designed mRNA sequence exhibited favorable predicted secondary structural characteristics; however, further experimental evaluation is required to assess translational efficiency and stability. Although this study is limited to computational analyses and requires experimental validation, the findings suggest that PV-GNProtecta may represent a potential candidate for further investigation against PUUV infection.

analysis.background: Puumala virus (PUUV) is the main cause of nephropathia epidemica, a zoonotic disease with renal complications and no approved vaccine, representing a significant public‑health threat.
analysis.methods: An immunoinformatics workflow was used to design an mRNA multi‑epitope vaccine (PV‑GNProtecta) from conserved glycoprotein G and nucleoprotein N regions, selecting highly antigenic, non‑allergenic T‑ and B‑cell epitopes, adding adjuvants, performing codon optimization for E. coli expression, structural modeling, docking to TLR4, 100 ns molecular‑dynamics simulation, and immune‑simulation.
analysis.results: The construct contained highly antigenic, non‑allergenic epitopes; population‑coverage analysis indicated broad HLA responsiveness; physicochemical assessment showed stability and solubility; 95.5 % of residues were in favored Ramachandran regions with an ERRAT score of 91.4; docking and MD predicted stable interaction with TLR4; immune simulation suggested elevated IgG, IFN‑γ and IL‑2 responses.
analysis.contribution: The study delivers a complete in‑silico pipeline and a promising mRNA vaccine candidate for PUUV, providing a basis for subsequent experimental validation.
analysis.limitations: Results are limited to computational predictions; experimental work is needed to confirm translational efficiency, stability, and immunogenicity, and only an abstract is available.

analysis.summary_en: Background: Puumala virus causes nephropathia epidemica and lacks an approved vaccine, posing a public‑health risk. Methods: Researchers used immunoinformatics to design an mRNA multi‑epitope vaccine (PV‑GNProtecta) from conserved PUUV proteins, selecting antigenic, non‑allergenic epitopes, adding adjuvants, optimizing codons, modeling structure, docking to TLR4, running 100 ns MD, and simulating immunity. Results: The construct showed high antigenicity, broad HLA coverage, stable physicochemical properties, 95.5% favored Ramachandran residues, ERRAT 91.4, favorable TLR4 interaction, and predicted IgG, IFN‑γ, IL‑2 increases. Contribution: Provides a full in‑silico pipeline and a candidate vaccine for further experimental study. Limitations: Findings are purely computational; experimental validation is required, and only an abstract was reviewed.

papers.title: Human febrile illness associated with Yanggou tick virus: Clinical characteristics and epidemiological links to rodents.
papers.abstract: Objectives We identified Yanggou tick virus (YGTV), a segmented flavivirus previously unrecognized as a human pathogen, in a patient presenting with fever and headache. This study aims to characterize the epidemiology and clinical manifestations of YGTV infection in patients with fever of unknown origin (FUO). Methods We conducted a surveillance study at the First Hospital of Jilin University (2020-2025) involving 1011 patients with FUO. Concurrently, ticks and rodents in the vicinity of the patients' residences and workplaces were collected for viral detection. YGTV infection was confirmed via PCR assays. Positive samples were used for viral isolation, genome amplification, and phylogenetic characterization. An Apodemus agrarius challenge model was established to evaluate viral persistence and shedding. Results Of the 30 confirmed cases of YGTV infection, 10 were co-diagnosed with hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome (HFRS). The patients showed no clear seasonality or geographic bias. Notably, rodent contact (43.3%) was a more frequent risk factor than tick bites (6.7%). While clinical presentations were non-specific, nearly 50% of the patients presented with gastrointestinal and neurological symptoms. YGTV was isolated from patients, ticks, and A. agrarius (the latter often co-infected with Hantaan virus). Animal models confirmed persistent splenic infection and viral shedding via oral and fecal routes. Conclusion Our findings establish YGTV as an underdiagnosed cause of human febrile illness, underscoring the transmission risks posed by tick vectors and rodent reservoirs. These results highlight the urgent need for enhanced clinical surveillance and diagnostic screening among patients presenting with FUO, particularly in regions where the virus is endemic.

This study aims to characterize the epidemiology and clinical manifestations of YGTV infection in patients with fever of unknown origin (FUO). Methods We conducted a surveillance study at the First Hospital of Jilin University (2020-2025) involving 1011 patients with FUO. Concurrently, ticks and rodents in the vicinity of the patients' residences and workplaces were collected for viral detection. YGTV infection was confirmed via PCR assays. Positive samples were used for viral isolation, genome amplification, and phylogenetic characterization. An Apodemus agrarius challenge model was established to evaluate viral persistence and shedding. Results Of the 30 confirmed cases of YGTV infection, 10 were co-diagnosed with hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome (HFRS). The patients showed no clear seasonality or geographic bias. Notably, rodent contact (43.3%) was a more frequent risk factor than tick bites (6.7%). While clinical presentations were non-specific, nearly 50% of the patients presented with gastrointestinal and neurological symptoms. YGTV was isolated from patients, ticks, and A. agrarius (the latter often co-infected with Hantaan virus). Animal models confirmed persistent splenic infection and viral shedding via oral and fecal routes. Conclusion Our findings establish YGTV as an underdiagnosed cause of human febrile illness, underscoring the transmission risks posed by tick vectors and rodent reservoirs. These results highlight the urgent need for enhanced clinical surveillance and diagnostic screening among patients presenting with FUO, particularly in regions where the virus is endemic.

papers.title_zh: 与羊沟蜱病毒相关的人类发热疾病:临床特征及与啮齿动物的流行病学关联

analysis_zh.background: 研究确定黄沟蜱病毒(YGTV),一种分段的黄病毒,作为此前未被识别的人类致病菌,可导致发热和头痛。
analysis_zh.methods: 在吉林大学第一医院(2020‐2025)开展的监测研究纳入了1011例原因不明的发热患者;采集患者居住地附近的蜱和啮齿动物并通过PCR检测,阳性样本用于病毒分离、基因组扩增、系统发育分析,以及使用田野鼠(Apodemus agrarius)挑战模型评估持续感染和排泄情况。
analysis_zh.results: 共鉴定出30例YGTV阳性病例,其中10例合并诊断为肾综合征出血热;未观察到明显的季节性或地域偏倚;啮齿动物接触(43.3%)比蜱叮咬(6.7%)更常见为风险因素;约50%的患者出现胃肠和神经系统症状;YGTV从患者、蜱和田野鼠中分离,且常与汉滩病毒共同感染;动物模型显示脾脏持续感染并通过口腔/粪便排泄。
analysis_zh.contribution: 研究结果确认YGTV是人类发热疾病的漏诊原因,并强调蜱媒介和啮齿动物储存宿主的传播风险,凸显在流行地区对原因不明发热患者加强临床监测和诊断筛查的必要性。
analysis_zh.limitations: 在提供的证据中未报告。

papers.title: DNA and mRNA Vaccines Against Hantaviruses: Antigen Design, Delivery Strategies and Translational Progress.
papers.abstract: Hantaviruses are members of the Hantaviridae family, which can cause hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome (HFRS) and hantavirus cardiopulmonary syndrome (HCPS). At present, no specific antiviral treatment is available for hantavirus infection, while licensed hantavirus vaccines are restricted to a limited number of countries in Asia. This review summarizes recent advances in hantavirus deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA) and messenger RNA (mRNA) vaccines, focusing on antigen design, delivery systems, immunogenicity, safety and translational development. Peer-reviewed studies published primarily within the past 10 years were evaluated together with available hantavirus vaccine trials registered in ClinicalTrials.gov, with emphasis on Hantaan virus (HTNV), Puumala virus (PUUV) and Andes virus (ANDV). DNA vaccine candidates have demonstrated immunogenicity in preclinical and early clinical studies, with an acceptable safety profile. mRNA vaccines represent a newer approach with promising preclinical evidence of humoral and cellular immune responses. However, they have not yet been evaluated clinically. Studies have also reported the potential for varying degrees of cross-protection between hantavirus species, although protection remains limited by antigenic diversity. Overall, current evidence supports further development of nucleic acid-based hantavirus vaccines, particularly multivalent strategies, with emphasis on standardized evaluation and clinical efficacy.

analysis.background: Hantaviruses cause hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome and hantavirus cardiopulmonary syndrome, yet no specific antivirals exist and licensed vaccines are limited to a few Asian countries. (A1, A2)
analysis.main_directions: The review summarizes recent DNA and mRNA vaccine designs, delivery platforms, immunogenicity, safety, and translational progress, emphasizing emerging mRNA approaches. (A3, A6)
analysis.current_state: DNA vaccine candidates have shown immunogenicity and acceptable safety in preclinical and early clinical studies; mRNA vaccines elicit strong humoral and cellular responses in animals, but none have yet entered clinical trials. (A5, A6, A7)
analysis.gaps: Cross‑protection is limited by antigenic diversity, and the absence of clinical evaluation for mRNA vaccines leaves efficacy uncertain; the evidence base relies mainly on recent studies and registered trials. (A8, A7, A4)
analysis.future_research: Future work should develop multivalent nucleic‑acid vaccines, adopt standardized immunogenicity assays, and conduct definitive clinical efficacy trials. (A9)

analysis.summary_en: Background: Hantaviruses cause severe HFRS and HCPS, with no antivirals and limited licensed vaccines (A1, A2). Main directions: The review covers DNA and mRNA vaccine design, delivery, immunogenicity, safety, and translational progress, highlighting mRNA advances (A3, A6). Current state: DNA vaccines are immunogenic and safe in early studies; mRNA vaccines show strong preclinical responses but lack clinical testing (A5, A6, A7). Gaps: Antigenic diversity restricts cross‑protection and mRNA vaccines lack clinical data; evidence is confined to recent studies and trial registries (A8, A7, A4). Future research: Pursue multivalent nucleic‑acid vaccines, standardized evaluation, and robust clinical efficacy trials (A9).

papers.title_zh: DNA和mRNA疫苗针对汉坦病毒:抗原设计、递送策略与转化进展

analysis_zh.background: 汉坦病毒导致肾综合征出血热和汉坦病毒心肺综合征,但尚无特异性抗病毒药物,且获批疫苗仅限于少数亚洲国家。(A1, A2)
analysis_zh.main_directions: 本综述概述了近期DNA和mRNA疫苗的设计、递送平台、免疫原性、安全性及转化进展,重点强调新兴的mRNA方法。(A3, A6)
analysis_zh.current_state: DNA疫苗候选物在临床前和早期临床研究中显示出免疫原性和可接受的安全性;mRNA疫苗在动物中诱导强烈的体液和细胞免疫应答,但尚未进入临床试验。(A5, A6, A7)
analysis_zh.gaps: 交叉保护受抗原多样性限制,且缺乏mRNA疫苗的临床评估导致其有效性不确定;证据基础主要依赖近期研究和已登记的试验。(A8, A7, A4)
analysis_zh.future_research: 未来工作应开发多价核酸疫苗,采用标准化的免疫原性检测,并开展确定性的临床疗效试验。(A9)

papers.title: Epidemiology and Economic Burden of Puumala Virus Infection in Styria, Austria, 2003 to 2024
papers.abstract: Background Hantavirus infections cause hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome and impose a potential burden on healthcare systems. However, comprehensive economic data remain scarce. We quantified the inpatient economic burden of hospitalized patients with Puumala virus (PUUV) infections in Styria, Austria's primary endemic region, to identify hospitalization costs and early admission predictors of costs. Methods This retrospective cost-of-illness study analyzed 1049 serologically confirmed PUUV hospitalizations across 20 public hospitals in Styria, Austria between September 2003 and March 2024. Costs were estimated using the Austrian performance-oriented hospital financing (Leistungsorientierte Krankenanstaltenfinanzierung) diagnosis-related group system, standardized to 2024-equivalent Euros using consumer price index deflation. Admission predictors of cost were assessed using multivariable γ-generalized linear modeling with multiple imputations. Temporal trends in length of stay were analyzed using weighted segmented linear regression. Results Cumulative inpatient cost was ∼€10.3 million (mean per-case: €9788) for the entire study period of 21 years. Three epidemic years (2012, 2019, and 2021) accounted for 53.6% of cases and over €5.2 million in expenditure, with peak annual costs reaching €1.93 million (0.274% of total Styrian inpatient expenditure) in 2012. Prolonged activated partial thromboplastin time (aPTT; cost-ratio 1.024 per second, 95% CI 1.019-1.030) and older age (CR 1.004 per year, 95% CI 1.001-1.008) were independent admission-level predictors of higher cost. Median hospital length of stay declined by ∼50% over the study period. Conclusions PUUV hospitalizations impose a sharply episodic but recurrent economic burden on regional healthcare systems. Admission aPTT and age independently predicted cost, but clinical outcomes were not modeled and these variables do not constitute a triage tool. Epidemic preparedness strategies are warranted.

analysis.background: Hantavirus infections cause hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome and impose a potential burden on healthcare systems; comprehensive economic data on Puumala virus (PUUV) infection are scarce.
analysis.methods: A retrospective cost‑of‑illness study analyzed 1,049 serologically confirmed PUUV hospitalizations across 20 public hospitals in Styria, Austria (Sept 2003–Mar 2024); costs were estimated using the Austrian DRG system and standardized to 2024‑Euro values; admission cost predictors were evaluated with multivariable γ‑generalized linear modeling and multiple imputation; temporal trends in length of stay were examined via weighted segmented linear regression.
analysis.results: Cumulative inpatient cost was ≈€10.3 million (mean €9,788 per case); three epidemic years (2012, 2019, 2021) accounted for 53.6% of cases and >€5.2 million, with a peak annual cost of €1.93 million in 2012; prolonged aPTT (cost‑ratio 1.024 per second, 95 % CI 1.019‑1.030) and older age (CR 1.004 per year, 95 % CI 1.001‑1.008) independently predicted higher cost; median hospital length of stay declined by ~50% over the study period.
analysis.contribution: The study quantifies the inpatient economic burden of PUUV in Austria, identifies admission‑level predictors of higher cost, and underscores the episodic yet recurrent financial impact, providing evidence for regional epidemic preparedness and resource planning.
analysis.limitations: Clinical outcomes were not modeled, limiting insight into cost‑outcome relationships; the analysis is based on abstract‑only information.

analysis.summary_en: Background: Hantavirus infections cause hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome and may burden healthcare, yet PUUV economic data are scarce. Methods: Retrospective cost‑of‑illness study of 1,049 PUUV hospitalizations in Styria (2003‑2024) used Austrian DRG costing, γ‑GLM with imputation for predictors, and segmented regression for LOS trends. Results: Total inpatient cost ≈€10.3 M (mean €9,788); three epidemic years contributed 53.6% of cases and >€5.2 M, with peak €1.93 M in 2012; longer aPTT and older age independently raised costs; median LOS fell ~50%. Contribution: Provides first comprehensive PUUV inpatient cost assessment in Austria, identifies cost predictors, and informs preparedness. Limitations: Clinical outcomes not modeled and findings derive from abstract‑only data.

papers.title_zh: 2003至2024年奥地利施蒂利亚地区普马拉病毒感染的流行病学与经济负担

analysis_zh.background: 汉坦病毒感染导致肾综合征出血热,并对医疗系统构成潜在负担;关于普马拉病毒(PUUV)感染的全面经济数据稀缺。
analysis_zh.methods: 一项回顾性疾病成本研究分析了奥地利施蒂利亚地区20家公立医院在2003年9月至2024年3月期间的1,049例血清学确诊的PUUV住院病例;费用采用奥地利DRG系统估算并标准化为2024欧元;入院费用预测因素通过多变量γ广义线性模型和多重插补评估;住院时长的时间趋势使用加权分段线性回归进行检验。
analysis_zh.contribution: 本研究量化了奥地利PUUV住院经济负担,识别了导致费用升高的入院层面预测因素,并强调了其间歇性但反复出现的财政影响,为地区流行准备和资源规划提供了依据。
analysis_zh.limitations: 未对临床结局进行建模,限制了费用与结局关系的洞察;分析仅基于摘要信息。

papers.title: Seasonal Dynamics, Host Network Structure, and Environmental Drivers of Gamasid Mite Communities on Small Mammals in a Dry-Hot Valley: A Year-Round Monitoring Study.
papers.abstract: Ectoparasitic gamasid mites on small mammals play crucial roles in transmitting zoonotic pathogens like hantaviruses associated with hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome (HFRS). To elucidate their community, network structure, and seasonal drivers in xeric habitats, a consecutive 12-month localized survey was conducted in Waxi Village, Binchuan County, a dry-hot valley in Yunnan Province, southwest China, from November 2020 to October 2021. From 1329 captured small mammals (18 species, 89.62% rodents), 12,075 gamasid mites belonging to 33 species were identified. The community exhibited overwhelming dominance by the family Laelapidae (Cr = 99.35%) and genus Laelaps (Cr = 97.37%). Laelaps algericus, L. guizhouensis, and L. nuttalli constituted the dominant mite species (cumulative Cr = 88.96%) and formed a tightly correlated core species cluster. Overall infestation prevalence (PM), mean intensity (MI), and mean abundance (MA) were 46.05%, 19.73 mites/host, and 9.09 mites/host, respectively. The bipartite host-gamasid network revealed a significantly nested architecture (NODFobs = 31.16, Z = 14.03, p < 0.001) with high specialization (H2' = 0.599), anchored by dominant hosts (Rattus andamanensis, Apodemus chevrieri, and Mus caroli). α-diversity analysis showed that Margalef richness, Shannon-Wiener index, and Gini-Simpson index peaked in autumn (November), while troughs occurred in mid-spring (April) and mid-autumn (October). Non-metric multidimensional scaling (NMDS, stress = 0.0048) and PERMANOVA (R2 = 0.074, p = 0.001) confirmed significant seasonal shifts in community composition. Standard redundancy analysis (RDA) suggested temperature as the primary climatic driver (F = 7.205, p = 0.001; total model explanation = 8.2%). However, partial RDA (pRDA) conditioning on host species identity demonstrated that climatic variables directly accounted for only 0.1% of net variance (F = 0.662, p = 0.521). Our findings indicate that gamasid mite community assembly in this dry-hot valley is characterized by strong species dominance and network nestedness and that seasonal fluctuations are consistent with a host-mediated pattern rather than being directly governed by climate.

analysis.summary_en: Background: Ectoparasitic gamasid mites on small mammals are key vectors for zoonotic pathogens such as hantaviruses linked to hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome. Methods: A consecutive 12‑month survey was carried out in Waxi Village, Binchuan County, Yunnan Province, China, from November 2020 to October 2021, capturing 1,329 small mammals (18 species, 89.62 % rodents) and identifying 12,075 gamasid mites across 33 species. Results: The mite community was dominated by Laelapidae (Cr = 99.35 %) and Laelaps (Cr = 97.37 %), with Laelaps algericus, L. guizhouensis, and L. nuttalli comprising 88.96 % of individuals; overall infestation prevalence was 46.05 %, mean intensity 19.73 mites/host, and mean abundance 9.09 mites/host. The bipartite host‑mite network was significantly nested (NODFobs = 31.16, Z = 14.03, p < 0.001) with high specialization (H2′ = 0.599). Alpha‑diversity indices peaked in autumn (November) and dipped in mid‑spring (April) and mid‑autumn (October). NMDS (stress = 0.0048) and PERMANOVA (R² = 0.074, p = 0.001) confirmed seasonal shifts in community composition. Redundancy analysis identified temperature as the primary climatic driver (F = 7.205, p = 0.001, total model explanation = 8.2 %), but partial RDA conditioning on host species showed climatic variables explained only 0.1 % of variance (F = 0.662, p = 0.521). Contribution: The study demonstrates that gamasid mite community assembly in a dry‑hot valley is dominated by a few species, exhibits a nested network structure, and that seasonal dynamics are driven more by host community changes than by climate, informing surveillance of zoonotic disease risk. Limitations: not reported in the supplied evidence.
